editorial.headline: Sharia Banking Beyond the Payments Rail
editorial.standfirst: This activity is open to full foreign ownership nationally and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali, where its large-scale risk classification places it outside the moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 64124 covers forms of sharia banking that sit outside the general banking system. Its work has two connected sides: gathering money from the public as deposits and/or investments, then distributing it to the public as financing and/or other sharia-based forms. The boundary is important. This activity does not provide payment-traffic services, including fund-transfer services. It is therefore banking based on sharia principles that channels public funds into financing, without operating a payments-transfer function.

The scope expressly includes the model of a Bank Perekonomian Rakyat Syariah, including Bank Perkreditan Rakyat Syariah. What matters is the underlying activity: receiving public deposits or investments and extending sharia-based financing or other sharia-based forms to the public. The record opens that activity at every listed business scale—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar—so the classification is not confined to one size of enterprise.

At the national level, the PMA position remains TERBUKA and allows foreign ownership up to 100%. The national ceiling is 100%, so foreign ownership can reach full ownership nationally. The stated basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-backed registration, that is the central national fact: this code is open, and the record gives no national foreign-share cap below full ownership.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion on the supplied record. The activity is not blocked for PMA registration under the island-wide, permanent Bali moratorium and is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The specific reason is its OSS risk classification at the Besar scale: Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, or Medium-High/High. That classification is given as the reason the activity is not blocked by the moratorium. The Bali record states no separate Bali foreign-ownership percentage, local-partnership requirement, or other Bali-side condition for this activity. On these facts, the Bali position is genuinely open rather than an apparent opening concealing a registration block.
